name: rtx2060s
description: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 SUPER (TU106, Turing, sm_75) at its 1470 MHz base clock: one Vortex core per SM; the SM is the RTX 2060's (rtx2060).

sources.SM (all core knobs): Inherited from rtx2060: the same TU106 SM
sources.NUM_CORES: 34 SMs, 2176 CUDA cores (GeForce RTX 2060 SUPER specifications)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS: 4 MB L2 (TU106 with all eight 32-bit memory controllers): 16 ways over power-of-two sets
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_DATA_RATE, PLATFORM_MEMO: 256-bit GDDR6 at 14 Gbps: 16 x16 channels at 14000 MT/s, 16 x 2 B x 14 GT/s = 448 GB/s
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE: 1470 MHz base clock (1650 MHz boost); Accel-Sim's SM75_RTX2060_S configuration runs it at 1905 MHz
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies inherited from rtx2060 (Jia et al.'s T4, the same Turing SM, L1 and L2 design); Accel-Sim's SM75_RTX2060_S configuration is tuned to 20 (L1) and 160 (L2) cycles
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY, PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: Inherited from rtx2060 (calibrated to the T4's measured 188 and 296 cycles: the same Turing SM-to-L2 network and GDDR6)
sources.L2_MSHR_SIZE: 64 per bank: Little's law on the 108-cycle L2-miss round trip x 305 B/cycle (448 GB/s / 1470 MHz) / (16 banks x 64 B) = 32.1, rounded up to a power of two
